# Caddy — root-context-sse

App at /, proxy at /, PUSH over Server-Sent Events. Caddy relays an upgrade with no configuration and has no switch to stop it, so the refusal is written out: a request carrying an Upgrade header is answered 501, which means the failure comes from the proxy rather than from Atmosphere.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/templates/passthrough-sse.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# passthrough.caddyfile, through a proxy that refuses to upgrade a connection.
#
# The Apache and NGINX *-sse configs refuse by omission: Upgrade and Connection
# are hop-by-hop headers neither forwards unless a directive puts them back.
# Caddy relays an upgrade with no configuration and has no switch to stop it, so
# the refusal is written out — and the 501 then comes from the proxy rather than
# from Atmosphere, the same answer HAProxy gives.
#
# SSE still works, because it is an ordinary HTTP GET that streams
# text/event-stream, and the client-to-server messages are POSTs to the same
# path. Selecting a WebSocket transport here fails, which is the point of the
# scenario rather than a bug.
:80 {
	import common

	@upgrade header Upgrade *
	respond @upgrade 501

	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
